Free Salary Slip Generator India 2025 (Payslip Creator)

Generate formal, compliant monthly salary slips (payslips) for employees, startups, small businesses, and freelancers across India. Auto-calculate gross salary, net take-home salary, EPF, Professional Tax (PT), HRA, and TDS.

Salary Structure Breakdown (Gross vs Net Take-Home)

Net Salary (Take-Home) = Total Earnings (Gross) - Total Statutory Deductions
  • 📌 Gross Earnings: Basic Salary + HRA + Special Allowance + Conveyance + Performance Bonus.
  • 📌 Statutory Deductions: EPF (12%) + Professional Tax (₹200/mo) + TDS (Tax Deducted at Source).

Standard CTC Component Distribution Rules

Basic Salary (40% - 50% of CTC)

The core taxable base of your compensation package upon which PF and Gratuity contributions are calculated.

House Rent Allowance HRA (50% of Basic)

Exempt from income tax up to limits set under Section 10(13A) for metro and non-metro cities.

Employee Provident Fund EPF (12%)

Statutory retirement savings deducted from basic salary and deposited into government EPFO account.

Professional Tax PT (State Slabs)

State-level tax deducted monthly (typically ₹200/month in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu).

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What are the essential components of a legal salary slip in India?

A valid salary slip must feature 2 main columns: Earnings (Basic Salary, HRA, Dearness Allowance, Special Allowance) and Deductions (Employee Provident Fund EPF, Professional Tax PT, Income Tax TDS, ESIC).

Is a salary slip required for home loan applications?

Yes! Banks (SBI, HDFC, ICICI) require 3 to 6 months of authorized salary slips along with Form 16 as official proof of income when evaluating home loan and personal loan applications.

💼 Salary Slip Component Breakdown (CTC vs In-Hand Salary)

A monthly salary slip issued by an employer is a vital financial document required by employees for home loans, personal credit cards, income tax filing (Form 16), and job switches. Understanding the distinction between Gross Earnings and Statutory Deductions is essential for every salaried professional in India.

Standard Salary Earnings Components:

  • Basic Salary: Core taxable component, typically 40% to 50% of Total CTC.
  • House Rent Allowance (HRA): Tax-exempt allowance under Section 10(13A) of Income Tax Act based on rent paid.
  • Special / Dearness Allowance: Supplementary allowance provided to balance inflation and living costs.

Mandatory Statutory Deductions:

  • Employee Provident Fund (EPF): 12% contribution of Basic Salary deducted under EPF Act 1952.
  • Professional Tax (PT): State-level tax (typically Rs. 200/month in Maharashtra, Karnataka, WB).
  • TDS (Tax Deducted at Source): Monthly income tax withheld under Old or New Tax Regime slabs.
